messages:
alyssa: Heads up — observed a ~12-18% tail-latency regression for Mixtral-MQA after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak (prefer fused FMA path). Repro on staging with long chat workload. @ben @carmen can you take a look?
ben: Do we have a profile capture? link to the perf dashboard or raw numbers would help :eyes: 
alyssa: Pasted the profiling dump I pulled from staging below (seq=1024, batch=8, sustained load). Not pretty. @profiling-bot posted the run.
profiling-bot: ```text
run_id=stg-2026-03-17-18:22
model=mixtral-mqa
seq_len=1024 batch_size=8 total_tokens=5120000
wall_time_s=420
latency_ms: p50=45 p95=210 p99=320
kernel_time_pct:
  matmul_fused_fma=42\%
  matmul_split=28\%
  kv_copy=12\%
  rope_scale_ops=6\%
  other=12\%
kv_cache_stats:
  avg_slots_per_page=128
  page_frag_ratio=0.41
  active_pages=94
  page_evictions=120
```
carmen: Interesting — avg_slots_per_page is low and page_frag_ratio is high. That smells like paged-KV fragmentation + more memcpy churn (kv_copy). Could be coming from num_key_value_heads mismatch or layout. What are the model config knobs? 
ben: Can you paste the config? Also, did kernel-selector fall back to the split matmul path because fused didn't support current RoPE scaling? 
alyssa: Config snippet from the staging bundle: ```python
# model-config.yaml
num_heads: 32
num_key_value_heads: 16
kv_dim: 64
rope_scaling: 0.98
kv_layout: paged
```
liam: If num_kv_heads != num_heads we will have fewer KV slots per page for MQA than GQA which explains avg_slots_per_page=128 vs expected ~256. Paged layout + many small active slots -> fragmentation. Also, I suspect the kernel selector saw rope_scaling != 1.0 and decided fused FMA wasn't safe, falling back to matmul_split which is slower and causes higher p99. We should log exact selector decision.
maria: I can confirm from earlier tests: mixtral-gqa (same hw/workload) shows much healthier KV stats. @profiling-bot can you paste the baseline GQA capture?
profiling-bot: ```text
run_id=stg-2026-03-10-09:14
model=mixtral-gqa
seq_len=1024 batch_size=8 total_tokens=5120000
latency_ms: p50=40 p95=180 p99=270
kernel_time_pct:
  matmul_fused_fma=35\%
  matmul_split=20\%
  kv_copy=6\%
  rope_scale_ops=4\%
  other=35\%
kv_cache_stats:
  avg_slots_per_page=256
  page_frag_ratio=0.12
  active_pages=48
  page_evictions=20
```
ben: kv_copy is roughly 2x higher in the MQA run (12% vs 6%). That aligns with fragmentation hypothesis. Also matmul_split up by ~1.4x. Two orthogonal things to try: 1) force fused kernel acceptance for scaled RoPE (if numerically safe), 2) try an aggressive batching policy to reduce memcpy proportion by amortizing KV ops. I'll prototype both.
alyssa: Quick microbench I ran locally with batching_policy=aggressive — showed improvement. Paste: ```bash
# local microbench
set batching_policy=aggressive
run_microbench --model=mixtral-mqa --seq=512 --batch=16
# result snippet
latency_ms: p95=160 (was 210)
kv_copy_pct -> 7\%
```
carmen: That helps but we need a smarter default. Aggressive batching helps throughput but hurts single-user latency in low-QPS apps. We should add a workload-aware heuristic: use aggressive when per-route token QPS > threshold or when page_frag_ratio > 0.25. Simple thresholding might be enough as a first pass.
liam: Also file a kernel-selector issue: when rope_scaling != 1.0 we should run a quick numeric check and allow fused FMA if error remains within tolerance. I suspect current selector assumes exact-rope path only. I'll open #2345 and add failing testcases.
maria: I'll run a small matrix overnight: varying num_key_value_heads=[8,16,32] kv_dim=[64,128] and kv_layout in [paged,tiled] across MQA/GQA and collect p95/p99 + kv_copy pct + page_frag_ratio. Will share CSV + notebook by EOD.
ben: I'll prototype a selector patch to gate fused kernel on a rope-scale epsilon check and a little runtime flag to force fused on staging. If the numeric diff < 1e-4 we enable path. Will also add a selector debug log to perf traces.
alyssa: Nice. Action items: ben -> PR for kernel selector + debug logs; carmen -> prototype workload-aware batching heuristic; maria -> run configuration matrix and share results; liam -> add pager compaction trial (try compact-on-evict heuristic). I'll follow up with a short doc summarizing trade-offs. Thanks all :thumbsup: 
profiling-bot: Summary posted to dashboard: https://dashboard.internal/r/redwood/perf/threads/1999990000 — includes the captures from above and the linked runs.
